guidance: Scaling estimate only: the affinity laws assume the same impeller geometry, a constant efficiency and a constant fluid density, and they say nothing about where the new curve meets the system curve. A speed change beyond about 20 percent or a trim beyond about 10 percent of the diameter needs the manufacturer's curve, and the motor, shaft, bearings and NPSH must be rechecked.
method: The affinity laws for one machine, the form Engineering ToolBox calls the specific centrifugal pump laws: a speed change n and an impeller diameter D move the duty point as Q2 = Q1 (n2/n1)(D2/D1), H2 = H1 (n2/n1)^2 (D2/D1)^2 and P2 = P1 (n2/n1)^3 (D2/D1)^3. The input is one measured point on the head-flow curve (flow in m3/h, head in metres of the handled fluid, shaft power in kW) together with the speed and impeller diameter it was measured at, plus the speed and diameter after the change; leaving the two diameters equal holds the wheel size, and leaving the speeds equal holds the shaft speed. The page reports the flow, head and power factors, the new duties, the percentage change in each, and the speed and diameter ratios, then scales from the new point to 50, 75, 100, 110 and 125 percent of the new speed so the shape of the new curve is visible. The head factor is exactly the square of the flow factor and the power factor its cube, which the tests assert as an invariant. The family form for geometrically similar pumps is a different set of exponents (flow as (n)(D)^3 and power as (n)^3 (D)^5) and is not used here, because changing the wheel diameter on an existing casing is the common field case. The laws assume the same impeller geometry, constant efficiency and constant fluid density; they give no system-curve intersection, so the real duty point is where the scaled machine curve meets the piping curve. A fan's static pressure in pascals is rho g H with rho about 1.2 kg/m3 for ambient air. A trimmed wheel is normally limited to about 10 percent of the diameter and a speed change to the motor and bearing limits, both of which are the manufacturer's data. Speeds are held between 1 and 60,000 rpm, diameters between 1 and 5,000 mm, flow between 0 and 10,000,000 m3/h, head between 0 and 100,000 m and power between 0 and 1,000,000 kW, and a value outside its range is refused with a sentence naming the field and the range. Values are shown to three significant decimals with thousands separators. Everything is computed in the browser; nothing is stored, uploaded or fetched.
